beats.lead: The most famous impostor in royal history
beats.text: Anna Anderson insisted she was Grand Duchess Anastasia Romanov.
beats.note: She surfaced in Germany in 1920, after a suicide attempt, and never once dropped the story.

beats.context: How long Anderson held to the claim, from 1920 until her death in 1984.

beats.lead: Science finally settled it in the 1990s
beats.text: DNA from Anderson's own body did not match a single Romanov.
beats.note: Tested from a tissue sample kept after a 1979 operation, and hair found in her late husband's book.

beats.name: Karl Maucher
beats.role: A relative of Franziska Schanzkowska, the Polish factory worker Anderson really was. His DNA matched Anderson's exactly, closing the case.

beats.text: The myth had somewhere real to hide. Two Romanov children's remains were not found until 2007.

beats.line: The evidence took decades to catch up with the myth.
